profiles.meeting_scenario: At a global bank's enterprise risk office, the quarterly systemic-risk dashboard has unexpectedly raised the 'required additional capital' figure for three broker-dealer subsidiaries by 28% after a weekend platform update, triggering concern from senior management before a board risk committee pre-read is sent out. The troubleshooting meeting is between the methodology lead who owns the systemic-risk measure and the delivery manager who owns the production pipeline. Their agenda is to determine whether the spike comes from the capital input mapping, the network exposure snapshot, the acceptability logic, or the diagnostic rerun process, and to agree on the immediate corrective action for the next overnight batch. The expected outcome is a shared plan for what to rerun, what data version to use, and what will count as the issue being resolved for the board package.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Macroprudential risk modeling, regulatory capital frameworks, contagion and network stress testing
members.background: Elena spent eight years at a central bank before joining the bank's quantitative risk team, where she led the design of the firm's systemic-risk measure based on capital allocations and an acceptability set used for internal macroprudential governance.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid a last-minute board escalation that makes the methodology look unstable, and she is especially worried that an implementation shortcut may have altered the meaning of the model without anyone noticing.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'capital allocation' in this workflow, they mean the legal-entity capital amounts after ring-fencing, internal netting constraints, and policy exclusions have already been applied.

The 'acceptable' status on the dashboard is supposed to reflect whether the full stochastic system outcome lies inside the approved regulatory acceptability set, not just whether summary indicators look normal.
The 'latest network snapshot' for quarter-end analysis is the close+2 approved exposure file that was signed off for model governance, even if later reconciled files exist.
A 'stress package rerun' means the full production-grade simulation with 5,000 Monte Carlo paths and endogenous contagion feedback, because only that reproduces the governed measure.

members.name: David Romero
members.expertise: Risk data pipelines, production model orchestration, financial systems integration and controls
members.background: David came from treasury technology and now manages the batch processes, data feeds, and operational controls that publish the bank's risk dashboards and committee packs.
members.private_state: He wants to restore stable overnight processing quickly and avoid reopening code that was already signed off for the quarterly release, while keeping the issue framed as a data/configuration matter rather than a platform defect.
hidden_assumptions: When the dashboard labels a field 'capital allocation,' it refers to the treasury feed's available entity capital balances before methodology-layer adjustments, because those adjustments are handled downstream or analytically.

An 'acceptable' result in operations means the dashboard falls back within the expected alert bands and reconciles to the control report, since that is what stakeholders use to decide whether the number is usable.
The 'latest network snapshot' is the most recently reconciled quarter-end exposure graph in the production store, which is the close+5 file that replaced the earlier cut automatically.

A 'stress package rerun' in troubleshooting means the standard diagnostic replay with cached scenarios, 500 paths, and fixed cascade order, because that is the safe and fast way to isolate operational issues.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss whether the spike is coming from the 'capital allocation' input
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means post-policy, post-ring-fencing legal-entity capital amounts that enter the systemic-risk optimization as admissible capital endowments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David means the raw treasury-sourced entity capital balances loaded into the production pipeline before methodology adjustments and exclusions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The dashboard and issue ticket already use the exact phrase 'capital allocation,' so each assumes the term is standardized and sees no reason to unpack a field name everyone uses daily.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'latest network snapshot' they are referring to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to validating against the 'latest network snapshot' for quarter-end
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is thinking of the close+2 approved exposure network that was frozen for methodology sign-off and board reporting consistency.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David is thinking of the close+5 reconciled exposure network that automatically replaced the earlier file in the production data store.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There is only one quarter-end cycle in view, so 'latest' sounds uniquely anchored; neither expects the other to be distinguishing between different dated versions within the same cycle.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the system being 'acceptable' again
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they need to get the result back to an 'acceptable' state before the board pack goes out
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the full simulated outcome distribution must fall back inside the approved acceptability set under the regulator-style stress framework used in the model documentation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David means the published dashboard should return to green/amber control bands and reconcile to the prior-quarter control report closely enough to release the board pack.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The system itself exposes a single 'acceptable/not acceptable' status, making it feel like a shared binary concept even though methodology and operations apply different underlying tests.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the next step is to 'rerun the stress package' tonight
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes a full production rerun using 5,000 paths, endogenous contagion feedback, and the capital-allocation optimization module enabled.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David assumes a diagnostic replay using 500 cached scenarios, fixed cascade order, and most heavy components disabled to meet the overnight window.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In day-to-day operations the phrase 'stress package' is used for both full production runs and quick diagnostics, and troubleshooting meetings often rely on that shorthand without restating run mode.

turns.inner_thought: That 28% jump right after the release is exactly the kind of thing that makes the board think the methodology is unstable. If the implementation path has started feeding the optimizer the wrong capital allocation definition, or if someone swapped out the approved close+2 quarter-end network, the governed measure is no longer the governed measure. And if the dashboard is calling something acceptable based on a shortcut instead of the actual acceptability set, we're flying blind.

turns.inner_thought: Fine, but the fastest way to isolate this tonight is the standard diagnostic replay.
